title: AI-assisted walkthroughs that prepare, transcribe and draft process narratives
problem: Walkthroughs, which trace one transaction end to end to confirm how a control works, are repeated every year even when processes barely change, and documenting them is tedious.
approach: PwC's Advanced Walkthrough Assistant ingests prior-year walkthroughs and drafts documentation for review; PwC said it will be used on 2026 year-end audits.
KPMG UK uses Clara AI to review control wording before walkthroughs and Copilot to transcribe them into flowcharts, where permitted.
The auditor performs the inquiry and observation; a reviewer approves the narrative, flowchart and design conclusion.
KPMG UK reports fewer meetings for control owners; PwC says busy-season savings are not that drastic yet (self-reported).

title: Test-of-design support and AI-drafted control test plans
problem: Breaking control descriptions into testable attributes and writing test plans is manual and uneven, and badly worded controls lead to follow-up requests and exceptions later.
approach: KPMG UK's Clara AI agents capture controls, draft a test plan for review and score control wording as decision support only.
Fieldguide and Petual agents draft test plans from the risk and control matrix; PwC's dynamic controls testing generates procedures that users review.
The auditor approves the test plan before testing runs and forms an independent view of design before comparing it with tool output.
KPMG UK says fuller attribute identification reduces follow-up requests, not quantified (self-reported).

title: Agent-assisted evidence requests and pre-submission evidence checks
problem: Chasing evidence is a main source of SOX delay: testers spend weeks requesting, chasing and re-requesting evidence from control owners across 20+ systems.
approach: Agents draft requests, check submitted evidence for completeness, file integrity and format, and help preparers fix gaps before submission.
Vendors describe next steps as pulling evidence through integrations and messaging control owners in Slack or Teams.
The control owner confirms submissions; the auditor determines sufficiency, not the platform.
Frazier & Deeter: evidence requests about 8% faster (19 hours) with Fieldguide (vendor-published); Optro claims fewer follow-ups, not quantified.

title: Risk-scored sample, coverage and control targeting
problem: Sample and coverage choices rely on static lists, geographic assumptions and hard-to-explain judgment, so testing effort follows rotation and habit rather than likely control breakdowns.
approach: Microsoft Internal Audit's Sample Selection Agent scores items on revenue, discounts, country risk and control indicators to produce a defensible risk-based selection.
Optro offers AI risk-based sample selection; KPMG describes predictive modelling of where control breakdowns are likely.
The audit lead approves the selection basis, threshold and any untested residual population.
Microsoft Internal Audit reports weeks of manual analysis cut to one day and ~2K hours/year saved (self-reported).

title: Agentic attribute testing of SOX key controls, with workpapers drafted for review
problem: Testers open PDFs, screenshots and exports for every sample, check each control attribute and document it by hand; KPMG's 2025 survey averages 16 hours per control.
approach: Agents read unstructured evidence, test each attribute with citations to source, and draft workpapers; exceptions route to a human reviewer.
Reddit's internal audit built this on Midship (now Optro Autonomous Testing); Klaviyo and Navan are other named users.
Reddit reports testing time down 60% per control (self-reported); 175 controls automated, over 40% of SOX scope (vendor-published).
People approve the test plan, sign off each conclusion and exception, and own deviation evaluation and deficiency classification.

title: Two-agent change-management testing for IT general controls
problem: Testing change-management controls means opening tickets across several systems with inconsistent formats, entering attributes in spreadsheets by hand and annotating evidence sample by sample.
approach: Microsoft Internal Audit built two Copilot Studio agents; one extracts tester, approver and dates from tickets into a table with pass/fail logic.
A second agent marks each extracted field on the source evidence so the reviewer sees where each attribute was validated.
Auditors review the audit table and exceptions; a reviewer samples the tick-marked evidence before sign-off.
Microsoft reports 850 hours/year and $185K/year saved, built and launched in 1-3 months (self-reported).

title: Matching client-provided evidence to selected samples with agents
problem: Each sampled control instance needs its supporting evidence traced to the sample and checked attribute by attribute, and evidence arrives in many formats, so manual tracing slows the test.
approach: Agents trace incoming documents to requested samples, extract and validate values, and record match or exception status with links to the source.
PwC said in October 2025 its controls-testing automation would work like Evidence Match; KPMG UK uses DataSnipper on IT change tickets.
The auditor reviews each exception and signs off the test.
No controls-specific result is published; RMF Audit & Control's roughly 50% saving is for invoice samples, not controls (vendor-published).
who: PwC, KPMG UK, DataSnipper, RMF Audit & Control

title: Full-population testing of transactional and master-data controls instead of samples
problem: Sample-based tests limit the conclusion to items examined and miss errors outside the sample; IFIAR recorded 24 insufficient-sample and 11 biased-sample findings in 2025.
approach: Extraction and matching agents, paired with deterministic code, test every item and link each value to its source.
Armanino with DataSnipper tests 100% of vendor master changes rather than a sample (vendor-published); the auditor reviews each match.
Microsoft Internal Audit agents test high-risk data sets in full; function-wide, report issuance fell from 3 to 2 weeks (self-reported).
Investigation thresholds are set before seeing output; the auditor investigates every flagged item or a justified subset; the partner approves evidential weight.
who: Armanino, DataSnipper, Microsoft Internal Audit, KPMG

title: Continuous, year-round control testing and monitoring instead of point-in-time cycles
problem: Testing bunched at interim and year-end finds failures months after they occur, often during the external audit, when remediation costs most and little time is left.
approach: Agents test controls as evidence arrives, and scheduled queries watch control data and route exceptions to owners.
Snowflake Internal Audit runs queries on Snowflake data through the Optro connector; Klaviyo tests throughout the year with Optro Autonomous Testing.
Owners triage each alert, people periodically review exceptions and agent configuration changes, and the auditor concludes on operating effectiveness.
Klaviyo and Snowflake report earlier issue detection and faster remediation, not quantified (vendor-published).

title: AI secondary review and multi-agent challenge of control-testing workpapers
problem: Manager review is a bottleneck, so small teams re-review only the riskiest workpapers and errors slip through; auditors are also less skeptical of work done by tools.
approach: FJ Management Internal Audit connects Claude to its Optro record; several models review each workpaper independently and disagreements are flagged.
A human checks each AI memo before it is attached; severity, materiality and sign-off stay with auditors.
FJ Management says memos caught actual defects and plans 100% secondary review (vendor-published, not quantified).
A research prototype, IntelliAudit, left 91.7% of final statuses unchanged on simulated organisations (independent); not accuracy against human auditors.
who: FJ Management, Optro, Microsoft, Tilburg University

title: AI-assisted testing in SOC 1, SOC 2 and ISAE 3402 service-auditor engagements
problem: Service-auditor engagements test high volumes of change-ticket evidence and rely on control owners' time; KPMG UK says demand for controls assurance reports nearly doubled.
approach: KPMG UK uses Clara AI agents for walkthrough preparation and test plans, DataSnipper to extract change tickets, and Copilot for workpaper drafting.
KPMG UK reports testing time about 18% lower on recent engagements, and about 15% lower with DataSnipper (self-reported).
The service auditor reviews all extracted data and conclusions; the opinion is unchanged.

title: AI drafting in the SOC cycle: system descriptions, evidence tracking, deviation responses
problem: Every SOC cycle, service organisations draft and update the system description, map it to the Trust Services Criteria, collect evidence snapshots and write management responses to deviations.
approach: GenAI turns process documents into draft control descriptions mapped to the criteria and drafts management responses covering root cause and remediation.
It also tracks evidence collection and project status and keeps continuous evidence snapshots.
Management owns the description and responses; the service auditor tests independently and evaluates deviations.
In a live poll at the 2026 EY SOC conference, 63% of attendees named evidence collection a top AI use case.

title: AI review of third-party SOC reports for reliance by user entities
problem: SOX programmes and user auditors read many vendor SOC reports to extract scope, test results, exceptions and complementary user entity controls, then map them to their own risk assessment.
approach: AI reads SOC reports, extracts test results, compares them with the user's risk assessment and prior periods, and flags deviations (EY speakers).
KPMG lists agents that manage SOC reports and extract control descriptions and test results.
The auditor or control owner concludes on reliance, evaluates deviations and tests user entity controls.
Described as a current application by EY and KPMG; no deployment figures found.

title: Compliance-automation platforms feeding SOC 2 examiners with continuously pulled evidence
problem: Clients submit dozens of screenshots and spreadsheets per SOC engagement, and SOC 2 is a gating requirement for enterprise sales, so speed is prized.
approach: Compliance-automation tools connect to the client's systems and pull evidence into a real-time dashboard that the CPA examiner tests against.
The debate is about where this automation replaces the examiner's own risk assessment and testing.
A licensed CPA designs and executes the tests and signs the opinion.
SOC leaders agree the tools make the process quicker; no figure is published (self-reported).
who: Unnamed SOC leaders and tool vendors

title: Testing controls that AI performs: AI-enabled controls as a new test object
problem: Clients now put GenAI and agents into financial-reporting processes, audit programmes mostly test around the AI, and there is no accepted method for testing a black-box control.
approach: Auditors scope AI components per use case and decide whether to rely on AI output, extending access and change controls to them.
AI-specific evidence includes lineage, per-inference logs and drift monitoring; COSO supplies control-testing templates for eight capability types.
KPMG UK is introducing a SOC 2+ opinion over AI governance and controls; the AICPA practice aid helps auditors understand AI-affected controls.
KPMG forecasts the first wave of AI-related material weaknesses in 2027 as programmes stop testing around AI (self-reported).

title: Firm-wide audit-platform agents extending into tests of controls in integrated audits
problem: External auditors repeat walkthroughs and tests of controls every year across large engagement portfolios at fixed or falling fees, and orchestrate tasks across many separate tools by hand.
approach: Network-wide agent frameworks extract data, analyse evidence, draft documentation and develop preliminary conclusions for professionals to review.
Deloitte Omnia agents run preliminary procedures; EY Canvas embeds agents; KPMG announced controls-testing agents as next; PwC plans controls-testing automation.
The engagement team reviews every agent conclusion and the partner signs the opinion.
EY covers about 130,000 assurance staff; Deloitte's framework reaches about 85,000 practitioners; PwC says year-one savings are not that drastic yet (self-reported).
who: Deloitte, EY, KPMG, PwC, Grant Thornton

title: AI-native audit pilot where agents test controls and balances on full populations
problem: Sampling-based audits spend most hours on data gathering and documentation rather than judgment.
approach: PwC Australia's AI-native audit platform has agents assess risk, plan audits and test balances and controls in real time on full populations.
Auditors handle context, communication and final judgments; human auditors oversee and validate all agent work.
The pilot starts with 5 audit clients, with all clients by 2028 and 1,600 auditors (self-reported plan).

title: Orchestrated agent swarms working alongside auditors in internal audit
problem: Prompt libraries plateau because nobody owns the prompts or measures their output, routines are built one by one, and one agent per task does not scale across an audit plan.
approach: PayPal Internal Audit describes swarm auditing: teams of agents orchestrated in parallel to run analytics and tests under a defined collaboration framework.
Scripts and agents built in audit are handed to first- and second-line owners; a separate bucket of hours covers experimentation.
Auditors remain the decision layer; agents are not replacing the team in the near term. No figures published (self-reported).

title: In-sourcing previously outsourced SOX and IT general controls testing to agents
problem: Many SOX programmes buy testing hours from co-sourcers; in KPMG's 2025 survey 58% said providers made up over 20% of SOX budget, and changing testers hurt consistency.
approach: Internal audit teams have agents run formerly outsourced tests, starting with IT general controls and then business-process controls, under their own review.
Havertys expects external spend to shift from testing hours to advisory work and starts with outsourced IT controls (vendor-published).
An unnamed Petual customer reportedly cut SOX budget to a quarter of its prior level (vendor-published, anecdotal).
An IT audit manager reviews every agent test result before acceptance.

title: Agent-delivered co-sourced and outsourced controls testing by audit and advisory firms
problem: Firms selling SOX and internal audit testing as a labour-based service face fee pressure and clients in-sourcing to agents, while unstructured evidence must still be read, matched and documented.
approach: RSM Beacon offers evidence validation, natural-language test steps and outputs traced to source; in August 2026 RSM announced an Andera AI alliance.
Riveron places agents at specific workflow steps, with a professional reviewing every result before it enters the workpaper.
Auditors approve, refine or intervene at key stages (RSM); open items are flagged to people.
Riveron measures review-ready workpapers, shorter cycles and earlier issue visibility rather than hours saved (self-reported); no figures.

title: Encoding SOX testing judgment into agent evaluation sets
problem: A model right 95% of the time is unusable if no one can tell which 5% to check, and agent conclusions must be defensible under PCAOB review.
approach: Vendors hire experienced SOX testers to write decision rules, define ground truth per control type and document failure modes.
Engineers use versioned evaluation sets to run regression tests before changing prompts, models or tools.
Experts sign off evaluation criteria before release; Fieldguide and Nace.AI recruit SOX experts for this (self-reported).

title: Idea: AI-assisted deviation evaluation and deficiency classification using a deviation memory
problem: Idea, not a deployment: classifying a failure as a minor gap, significant deficiency or material weakness depends on unwritten context; IFIAR recorded 11 findings in 2025.
approach: Teams would record why past exceptions were accepted in one repository.
An agent would check new exceptions against it and draft a classification once a human supplies context; the auditor classifies.
No deployment or measured outcome was found.

title: Idea: screen control evidence for AI fabrication and prompt injection before testing
problem: Idea, not a deployment: GenAI makes fake invoices, approvals and screenshots cheap, and control owners who know auditors use agents could hide instructions in evidence to steer them.
approach: Regulators and practitioners call for authenticity procedures: take evidence from source systems where possible, sanitise agent inputs and constrain outputs.
The auditor escalates suspected manipulation under the fraud standards; no public deployment of a dedicated screening step was found.
Survey: 65% of internal audit leaders cite fabricated documents as an AI fraud concern; 62% are unprepared or minimally prepared (independent).

title: Idea: external-auditor reliance on management's or internal audit's AI-enabled control testing
problem: Idea, not a deployment: reliance on others' testing is the main efficiency lever in SOX audits, but the standards predate AI and no public case was found.
approach: Practitioners and the IIA discuss parallel pilots with the external auditor and equal criteria for supervising AI-assisted work, whoever performs it.
KPMG argues full-population tools could lower the value of relying on management's tests, or raise it if its AI testing qualifies.
The engagement partner decides on reliance after evaluating competence, objectivity and the AI tool's certification; no measured outcome.

title: Idea: synthetic data and simulation agents to stress-test controls before ERP go-live
problem: Idea, not a deployment: the window between an ERP go-live or acquisition and a stable control environment is among the highest-risk periods, with controls untested against real volumes.
approach: KPMG proposes synthetic transaction populations and agents that simulate users and adversarial conditions to test access controls, approvals and rules before go-live.
COSO separately recommends test populations to validate AI accuracy and stress-test edge cases.
The ICFR lead or control designers approve scenarios and interpret failures; no measured outcome.
